title: Permutations (nPr)
tagline: Year 3 — Arrangements with and without repetition, restrictions, circular arrangements and digit problems

introduction.overview: A permutation is an arrangement in which order matters. The fundamental principle of counting says that if one task can be done in m ways and a second in n ways, the two together can be done in m × n ways. From it come the formulas for arranging r of n different objects (nPr), arranging objects when some are alike, arranging in a circle, and counting numbers formed from given digits under restrictions.
introduction.placementRelevance: Permutation questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds, typically as word arrangements, digit problems and seating with restrictions.
introduction.realWorldContext: Passwords, seat plans, schedules and license plates are counted with permutations.

learningObjectives: Use the multiplication principle and factorials
Use nPr and arrangements with identical objects
Handle restrictions (together, never together, fixed positions)

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: n! = n × (n − 1) × … × 1, with 0! = 1. Counting is by "choices in sequence": multiply the number of choices at each step.

coreDefinitions: Permutation of n distinct objects taken r at a time: nPr = n!/(n − r)!.
Arrangements of n objects with p alike of one kind, q alike of another: n!/(p! q!).
Circular arrangements of n distinct objects: (n − 1)!; if clockwise and anticlockwise are the same: (n − 1)!/2.
Treating items "together": glue them into one block, arrange the blocks, and arrange inside the block.
"Never together" = total arrangements − arrangements with them together.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Counting arrangements is filling positions one at a time: the first position has n choices, the next n − 1, and so on. Restrictions are handled by filling the restricted positions first.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Fill the most restricted position first, then the others. For "together" make a block; for "not together" subtract; for repeated letters divide by the factorials of the repeats.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Together / not together
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Together: (n − k + 1)! × k!;  Not together = total − together
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: ARRANGE with the two vowels together

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Digits
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Choices for each position, restricted first

mainNarrative: Count by positions. The number of ways to arrange 3 of 5 different letters is 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 = 5P3. If repetition is allowed, each position has 5 choices: 5³ = 125.
For words with repeated letters divide by the factorials of the repeats. The word LEVEL has 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5!/(2! 2!) = 30 arrangements.

For restrictions, fix the restricted items first. To arrange the letters of RAINBOW so that the vowels (A, I, O) are together, treat AIO as one block: 5 objects arranged in 5! = 120 ways, times 3! = 6 arrangements inside the block: 720.
For "never together", subtract. The total arrangements of 7 letters is 5040. With the three vowels together it is 720, so with the vowels not all together it is 5040 − 720 = 4320.
Circular arrangements fix one person to remove rotations: 6 people around a table can be seated in 5! = 120 ways; if two particular persons must sit together, treat them as a block: 4! × 2 = 48 ways.

deepDiveAspects.title: Digit problems
deepDiveAspects.content: For numbers, handle the leading digit first. 4-digit numbers from 0 to 9 without repetition: 9 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 4536.

deepDiveAspects.title: Rank of a word
deepDiveAspects.content: The position of a word in the dictionary order is found by counting the words that start with smaller letters at each stage.

solvedExamples.title: Arrangements with repeats
solvedExamples.question: How many different arrangements can be made from the letters of the word LEVEL?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Swapping identical letters does not give a new word.

solvedExamples.title: Together
solvedExamples.question: In how many ways can the letters of RAINBOW be arranged so that the vowels are together?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Arrange the blocks then the contents.

solvedExamples.title: Circular
solvedExamples.question: In how many ways can 6 people sit around a circular table if two particular people must sit together?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Fix a block and divide rotations.

steps.title: Block
steps.explanation: The pair is one unit: 5 units around a table: 4! = 24.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Pick the most restricted position, choose, then multiply the choices; use blocks and complements.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Counts must be divisible by obvious symmetry factors; reject non-integers.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Always ask which choice is most restricted.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Permutations connect to probability and seating puzzles.

advanced.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word ORANGE be arranged so that the three vowels occupy the odd positions (1st, 3rd and 5th)?
advanced.explanation: The vowels O, A, E take the 3 odd places in 3! = 6 ways and the 3 consonants take the even places in 3! = 6 ways: 36.

placementStyle.question: The number of 5-digit numbers divisible by 5 that can be formed from the digits 0 to 9 without repetition is
placementStyle.explanation: Units digit 0: 9 × 8 × 7 × 6 = 3024. Units digit 5: the leading digit cannot be 0 or 5, so 8 × 8 × 7 × 6 = 2688. Total 5712.

placementStyle.question: The number of arrangements of the letters of the word EXAMINATION is
placementStyle.explanation: There are 11 letters with A, I and N each repeated twice: 11!/(2! 2! 2!) = 4989600.

placementStyle.question: The rank of the word CAT among the arrangements of its letters in dictionary order is
placementStyle.explanation: The words in order: ACT, ATC, CAT, CTA, TAC, TCA. CAT is third (rank 3).
